Mogilny is 39 points in 26 games — elite current production that helps VAN win NOW, and the first-rounder cushions the long-term risk of a 35-year-old at $5.5M for two more years. Toronto saves $2.9M this season, sheds $11M of future liability, and gets the best player available who fills the structural toughness hole. Acceptance is uncertain because VAN is contending and may keep Bertuzzi for a playoff push.

recommendations.current: TOR first-round pick + TOR third-round pick
recommendations.summary: Acquire Shane Doan from Phoenix for Toronto's first-round and third-round picks if the Bertuzzi deal does not land; fills the same forward-toughness gap at lower cost.
recommendations.rationale: Phoenix are 9-13-4 with 14 expiring contracts, $47.81M payroll, and only $14.26M profit. They are in a full teardown and will sell Doan before he walks. Two picks for a 28-year-old 86-overall winger with 86 toughness and 91 checking is fair value for a seller. Payroll effect: -$2.4M to Phoenix, +$2.4M to Toronto. Acceptance is likely given their situation.

recommendations.summary: If all three fail, dress Tucker every night — 92 CHKG, 88 TOUG, 29, $1.3M — as the internal toughness band-aid.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker's 92 checking and 88 toughness are the closest things on the roster to what the coverage phase identified as missing. At $1.3M and only 3 games played, he is wasting away on the bench. He does not close the gap to the league's top tough forwards but prevents the structural hole from being exploited every night.

recommendations.summary: Move Koltsov up from the fourth line — he is producing at a point per game on the fourth line and needs to play where he is challenged.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 12 games (1.00 pts/game) at 8.8 minutes on the fourth line. No other fourth-liner is close to that rate. His development is capped by the quality of competition he sees.

recommendations.summary: Give Nash and his line more shifts per game — 23 points in 26 games on 12.9 minutes a night is top-six production on third-line ice.
recommendations.rationale: Nash is at 0.88 points per game at age 20 and playing only 12.9 minutes. He has earned more of the game. Prefer giving the line more ice over breaking it up, per the chemistry principle.

recommendations.summary: Safronov is 23 with POTE 91 and zero games played — he needs to be in the lineup or the GM needs to tell me why he is not.
recommendations.rationale: Three defencemen under 22 are playing regularly (Klesla 26 GP, Eminger 25 GP, Colaiacovo 11 GP). Safronov at 23 with a POTE of 91 and no games is a development asset sitting idle. Either dress him or tell me what I cannot see.

recommendations.summary: Spacek should be back in the lineup — 6 points in 11 games at 16 minutes a night does not justify a scratch.
recommendations.rationale: Spacek was earning 16 minutes a night and posting 0.55 points per game before being scratched. The production supports a roster spot. I cannot see the reason for the scratch, but the scoresheet disagrees with it.

recommendations.summary: Spezza stays on the fourth line until his production earns a move, regardless of his POTE.
recommendations.rationale: 11 points in 23 games on the fourth line is 0.48 per game — solid for that role, but the GM's standing instruction is that production drives the decision, not the scouting number. He moves when the points say so.

recommendations.summary: Chistov's scratch is correct — 4 points in 14 games at 9.5 minutes did not earn another spot.
recommendations.rationale: 0.29 points per game is below what the lineup needs from a forward. The production supports the decision to keep him out.

recommendations.summary: Watch Gaborik's minutes closely — if the drop from 18.8 to 14.0 holds past this week, he needs to be moved to a line that restores his ice.
recommendations.rationale: His season pace is 1.42 pts/g in 26 games but he managed zero in the last 2 and lost 4.8 minutes a game. At 22, a sustained minutes cut on a first-line producer is how development stalls. One data point, but it is the right direction to flag.

recommendations.summary: Chlup is trending up at 18 — 1.00 pts/g recently on rising minutes. Keep feeding him ice and reassess his line assignment in two weeks.
recommendations.rationale: 8 points in 13 games, then 2 in 2, and minutes up from 11.0 to 12.5. Small sample but the direction is right for an 18-year-old getting real minutes.

recommendations.summary: Roberts is 38 and just jumped to 22.0 mpg while his production fell to 0.50 pts/g. The GM should start planning for a minutes redistribution before the legs go.
recommendations.rationale: Season pace was 1.29 pts/g on 16.5 minutes; the last 2 games show 0.50 on 22.0. At 38 the body collects on 22-minute nights. This is not tonight's problem but it is a roster-planning problem.

recommendations.summary: Room is healthy at 14-2 with zero morale movement across the roster; no minutes changes needed.
recommendations.rationale: Every player's morale is unchanged since the last save. Lowest skater is Chlup at 82, who is getting minutes appropriate to his level. Sundin and Mogilny at 88 on 17.1 minutes are marginally under a 90+ band but stable and aging; better kept fresh.

recommendations.summary: Give Koltsov more of the game on the fourth line.
recommendations.rationale: 98 speed is our second-best on the roster. He is at 53 faceoffs and 54 toughness on a unit that has neither, so he needs game experience to grow into a role beyond raw speed.

recommendations.summary: Insert Tucker on L4 in place of the least productive skill forward.
recommendations.rationale: Tucker's 78 checking and 67 toughness raise the L4 mean from 56 to roughly 65 and give Koltsov a physical partner. The line currently has no one above 63 checking. If Tucker is a healthy scratch, he is the only roster fix for the bottom-six checking gap.

recommendations.summary: We need a centre who wins faceoffs. Only Sundin at 86 can.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 72, Chlup at 75, fourth-line centres at 52-53. We lose the draw on three lines every game. This forces our defencemen into coverage situations they should not face. A second reliable draw-winner is the single biggest roster addition this team needs.

recommendations.summary: Keep L1 as is.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin 86 faceoffs, Mogilny 88 scoring, Roberts 80 checking and 70 toughness, McCabe and Fischer 81 checking each. Balanced top line that can win draws, score, and handle a top opponent. Nothing on the sheet says change it.

recommendations.summary: Keep K1 as is despite Gaborik on the penalty kill.
recommendations.rationale: Fischer at 81 checking anchors it, Roberts at 80 adds a second body. Gaborik's 85 stamina lets him handle the shift and the game only pulls him for one PK shift per penalty, not the entire period. The unit mean of 75 checking is our best kill and both our top checkers are on it.

recommendations.summary: Start Belfour against New Jersey.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour reads 91 overall with morale 95; Aebischer is 84 at morale 80. The hardest matchup we have faced so far goes to the hotter goalie.

recommendations.summary: Take Colaiacovo off the first penalty kill and put McCabe on it against New Jersey's top power-play unit.
recommendations.rationale: NJ's PP has 8 goals on 52 chances, high volume, and Colaiacovo's penalty grade is 55, the lowest on our blue line. McCabe is 89 on penalties, the cleanest option to kill.

recommendations.summary: Leave the four forward lines as they are for this game.
recommendations.rationale: The lines behind a 10-game streak producing 6.9 goals and 1.4 against a night are settled, and New Jersey has no line weak enough to reward breaking up Gaborik's line or the Sundin line. The third line (Nash, Chlup, Upshall) is already our heaviest and rolls to start on their skill line.

recommendations.proposed: Todd Marchant / Alexei Zhamnov / Jozef Stumpel / Yanic Perreault
recommendations.summary: Acquire a top-nine centre at the deadline — Marchant, Zhamnov, Stumpel, or Perreault all carry one-year deals and could be available from non-contending clubs.
recommendations.rationale: Richards is at 27 points in 25 games on 16.8 minutes a night carrying the second line; Spezza (10 pts, 22 GP, 9.4 min) and Chlup (8 pts, 14 GP) are playoff third-liners on paper only. The Coach says this gap cannot be plugged internally.

recommendations.summary: Add a backup goalie before the deadline — a cheap veteran on a one-year deal or a young prospect for a late pick.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour is 39 with CONS 50 and a $6.50M expiring deal; if he goes down in April, Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) and Aebischer (26, $0.50M) are unproven in a playoff series.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Gaborik to a 5-6 year extension immediately at his next available opportunity.
recommendations.rationale: RW, 22 years old, $1.10M salary, expiring. He is the team's best offensive winger and his current pay is near-rookie level; every year he stays at that salary is a gift, and waiting only ratchets his demands.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Richards to a 5-6 year extension at his next opportunity.
recommendations.rationale: C, 24, $1.00M, 27 points in 25 games. Entering his prime on a contract that should not exist at this level. A six-year deal locks a top-two centre into the franchise.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Kaberle to a 5-6 year extension at his next opportunity.
recommendations.rationale: D, 26, $1.90M expiring. Entering his prime as the top-pairing defenceman; expect the raise to $3.5-4M but the term protects five years of a prime-year #1 D.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Nash to a 4-year extension.
recommendations.rationale: LW, 20, $1.20M. The Coach is trusting him on the first penalty kill at age 20 — that signals a player developing into a two-way contributor. Four years protects the development window without the full star commitment.

recommendations.summary: Keep Belfour through the playoffs, then offer two years at a reduced $3.5-4M salary; move him for a pick if he declines.
recommendations.rationale: 39 years old, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50 and POTE 50 say no upside and inconsistency risk. Still elite in core goalie grades (INTE 97, GSH_ 92, GSL_ 92) but paying $6.5M to a 39-year-old on a one-year ratchet is the classic mistake.

recommendations.summary: Offer Roberts a one-year deal at reduced salary, or move him at the deadline if a contender bites.
recommendations.rationale: LW, 38, $2.70M expiring. TOUG 92 and BALA 94 make him valuable in a playoff series, but at 38 there is no future here — one year at a discount or a rental-to-a-buyer for a pick.

recommendations.summary: Re-sign Svehla to two years at reduced salary (max $2.5M), or move him before expiry.
recommendations.rationale: D, 35, $3.60M expiring. ENDU 94 and CHKG 92 are still top-pairing numbers but POTE 55 and his age say decline is imminent. Two years caps the risk at one bad season.

recommendations.summary: Do not sell at the deadline.
recommendations.rationale: TOR is 18-5-0, first in the East by 3 points, with a +17-point gap to the ninth team. There is no scenario where selling helps this roster reach a Cup.

recommendations.summary: Dress Koltsov every night; he is producing at 1.09 ppg at age 23 with 92 speed.
recommendations.rationale: 12 points in 11 games is the best points-per-game on the roster among players under 30. Sitting a 23-year-old at 92 speed who is outproducing everyone except Mogilny/Sundin/Gaborik is wasted development and wasted offense.

recommendations.summary: Return Spacek to the lineup immediately — no injury, 84 playmaking, age 19.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach flagged this: 16 minutes a game to scratched with no injury. At 19 with 84 playmaking, every night he sits is a development night lost. He is the team's second-best young centre and should be eating minutes on the second or third line.

recommendations.summary: Remove Gaborik from the first penalty kill; his 98 speed and 92 playmaking are misallocated on a defensive unit.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik's value is offense and speed, not checking. Upshall (80 checking, age 21) or Fischer (82 checking, age 24) are better PK fits and both are young enough to develop the role. Cannot verify Nash's grades from the brief but the principle is sound.

recommendations.summary: Acquire a centre with 80+ faceoff (75 minimum) and ideally 80+ checking; cannot be fixed internally.
recommendations.rationale: Sundin (90 FO, age 33) carries the entire faceoff column alone. Richards is 70, Holden is 71. No internal rotation reaches 75. This is the single most impactful trade target: a two-way centre who wins draws and kills a shift addresses both the faceoff crisis and the thin checking column.

recommendations.summary: Toughness (zero at 80+) is a real gap but does not justify a move at 18-5-0 with playoff spot secure; revisit if first-round matchup is physical.
recommendations.rationale: Best toughness on the roster is McCabe 73. No one at 80+. However, the team is 18-5-0 with 40 points in 25 games and no urgency to spend a pick on a role player. If the first-round opponent is a heavy team, a rental enforcer from a non-playoff club could be addressed at the deadline with minimal cost.

recommendations.current: Nash, Gaborik, Richards, Upshall, Alexeev, Colaiacovo, Eminger (all 1yr)
recommendations.proposed: 5-6 year deals for the young core
recommendations.summary: Re-sign the expiring young core to 5-6 year term this summer, before the single-wave renewal ratchets their prices.
recommendations.rationale: 17 contracts expire for $28.60M, and the core (Gaborik 34 pts, Richards 27 pts, Nash 22 pts; Upshall/Colaiacovo/Eminger POTE 99) is in that group on $1.0-1.2M deals. The manual says lock stars on 5-6 years and avoid a same-summer cluster; re-signing early beats paying a career-year price.

recommendations.proposed: acquire a young centre at the deadline
recommendations.summary: At 18-5-0 we are buying, not selling: spend the Detroit first-rounder on a centre we keep, not a rental.
recommendations.rationale: We hold a first-rounder from Detroit plus our own 2nd-5th, and we are 40 points in 25 games — firmly in the race. The manual's deadline rule for a contender is to buy young players with potential over a first or second pick rather than rent and lose the chip.

recommendations.summary: At the deadline, pursue a young top-6 centre with a first or second-round pick; Richards (24, $1.00M) expiring makes this a double-purpose move.
recommendations.rationale: The Coach says we are thin at centre behind Sundin and cannot fix it internally. Richards is also expiring, so a deadline centre is both a playoff add and a succession plan. The Coach's read that internal shuffling cannot solve it is correct — we have no rostered centre aged 23 or under.

recommendations.summary: Do not re-sign Belfour (39, $6.50M) in the summer; if his grade is above 80, try to move him at the deadline for a draft pick rather than lose him for nothing.
recommendations.rationale: Belfour at 39 and $6.50M is the single largest salary on the roster. Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) is the successor at an eighth the cost. The guide's warning about losing good goalies by forgetting to re-sign applies to Tellqvist, not Belfour.

recommendations.summary: Keep Svehla, Roberts, and Renberg for the playoff run at the deadline even though all three are expiring and will not be re-signed.
recommendations.rationale: Svehla (35, $3.60M), Roberts (38, $2.70M), and Renberg (32, $2.00M) are useful depth for a team that is 18-5-0. Moving them for scraps at the deadline weakens the playoff roster; letting them walk in July saves $8.30M/year cleanly.

recommendations.summary: In the summer, sign Gaborik, Nash, Richards, Kaberle, Colaiacovo, and Eminger to 5–6 year deals and Chistov, Alexeev, Upshall, and Smirnov to 3–4 year deals to avoid a renewal cliff in 2010.
recommendations.rationale: Six players aged 19–21 all expire this summer. All six on six-year terms means they all come up again simultaneously — the guide warns about exactly this. Staggering three of them to 3–4 years means we re-evaluate three prospects in 2007 while locking in the other three at rookie-level salaries now.

recommendations.summary: Chara (27, 95 CHK, 94 TOUG, 31 pts/22 GP, $1.70M, 1 yr) fills the toughness gap (nothing above 73 on our roster) and the checking thinness simultaneously, and his 29 MPG gives us a true second top-pair option behind McCabe.
recommendations.rationale: OTT is 8-10-2, 22 pts, with 11 expiring contracts — they are rebuilding and Chara is on an expiring $1.7M deal, making him a first-round-and-a-prospect candidate. We hold a Detroit first plus second through fifth. The toughness column currently tops out at McCabe 73; Chara at 94 is a two-grade-level jump the roster cannot manufacture internally.

recommendations.summary: Avery (24, 93 face, 86 CHK, 88 SPD, $400K, 2 yrs) is the only young faceoff centre in the league who could become a keeper behind Sundin; LA is 6-10-5, 23 pts, out, with 13 expiring deals and Avery dressed at just 12 MPG.
recommendations.rationale: Richards at 70 faceoffs is our second-line centre and the Coach's flag is correct — the best available on the roster is Holden at 71. Avery at 93 faceoffs, 86 checking, 88 speed, age 24, $400K, two years controlled is the developmental answer. His 3 points in 24 games says he won't fix scoring, but fixing faceoffs and checking was the goal, not replacing Sundin.

recommendations.summary: Marchant (31, 94 face, 96 CHK, 85 SPD, 30 pts/24 GP, $4.88M, 1 yr) is the best available rental centre if we want to win now rather than develop — he wins draws, kills penalties, and scores at a second-line rate.
recommendations.rationale: CBJ is 6-11-1, 25 pts, clearly out, with 8 expiring contracts. Marchant is the single best two-way centre on the board (94/96/30 pts), but at 31 on $4.88M expiring he is a rental for April, not a re-sign target. Pair this interest with Avery — Marchant for now, Avery for later — rather than choosing one.

recommendations.summary: Belanger (27, 97 face, 83 CHK, $700K, expiring, 3 pts/24 GP) is the cheapest faceoff upgrade in the league and would fix every defensive-zone draw outside Sundin's line for $700K and a late-round pick.
recommendations.rationale: LA is 6-10-5, 23 pts, with 13 expiring contracts. At 97 faceoffs and $700K, Belanger is the lowest-cost solution to the faceoff crisis. He won't contribute offensively (3 points, 8 MPG) but he doesn't need to — he wins the draw and gets off the ice. Could be acquired alongside Avery from the same club to consolidate one negotiation.

recommendations.summary: Savard (27, 88 face, 86 SPD, 84 PASS, 24 pts/23 GP, $1.0M, 1 yr) is the most productive faceoff-capable centre on the market and is on the worst team in the league (5-16-1, 13 pts) with 11 expiring deals.
recommendations.rationale: Savard blends production (24 pts) with faceoffs (88) and speed (86) in a way no other available centre does. At $1M he is cheap. ATL is dead last and in full rebuild mode, so the question is whether they value a 27-year-old centre for a first or accept a second-plus-prospect. If they want too much, fall back on Belanger or Avery.

recommendations.summary: Conroy (33, 94 face, 89 CHK, 25 pts/25 GP, $2.0M, 1 yr) is the cheaper Marchant — same faceoff number, half the salary, two years older — a viable centre rental if Marchant's price is too high.
recommendations.rationale: CGY is 9-14-1, 21 pts, with 10 expiring contracts, clearly selling. At $2M he is far more absorbable than Marchant at $4.88M and still carries 94 faceoffs and 89 checking. At 33 he is a one-year rental with no future implications. The backup plan if Marchant and Savard are both too expensive.

recommendations.summary: Doan (28, 93 CHK, 98 TOUG, 88 fig, 16 pts/25 GP, $2.4M, 1 yr) brings the toughness column from a team-best 73 (McCabe) to 98 in one acquisition, at 28 and on an expiring deal from a club at 8-12-4.
recommendations.rationale: PHX is 22 pts, 8-12-4, out of the race, with 14 expiring contracts. Doan's 98 toughness is the highest available on the board by five points (next best is Chris Neil at 94). His faceoffs at 59 mean he plays wing not centre, but at 93 checking and 98 toughness he is a different kind of answer from anyone on our roster. 16 points is low but acceptable for a checking winger.

recommendations.summary: Jackman (23, 90 CHK, 89 TOUG, 15 pts/24 GP, 31 MPG, $700K, 3 yrs) is a young tough defenceman on a long cheap deal — but STL at 7-13-1 may prefer to keep a 23-year-old with three years left.
recommendations.rationale: At 23 with 90 checking, 89 toughness, 31 minutes a night, 15 points, and only $700K for three more years, Jackman is the long-term answer to the checking-thinness problem alongside Fischer (82 at 24). The risk is that rebuilding clubs keep their young defencemen, and STL has 9 expiring deals but may view Jackman as untouchable core.

recommendations.current: Marc Savard (ATL, C, 27, FACE 88, SPEE 86, PASS 84, 24 pts in 23 GP, $1.00M expiring)
recommendations.proposed: DET 1st round pick + Chistov (TOR, LW, 21, POTE 95, SPEE 89, 4 pts in 14 GP, $1.10M expiring) + TOR 3rd round pick
recommendations.summary: Acquire Marc Savard from Atlanta for the Detroit 1st, Chistov, and a 3rd. He is the only faceoff-capable centre producing at a point per game, and his contract term means we re-sign him on a 5-year deal before he tests the market.
recommendations.rationale: Savard's FACE 88 and 24 points in 23 games directly fix the gap the Coach flagged — Richards at FACE 70 cannot play second-line centre in the playoffs. Atlanta is dead last (13 pts, 5-16-1), carries 20 expiring deals worth $19.3M, and their $36.8M payroll against $34.4M revenue makes them cash-flow negative on a winning basis. A 1st + 3rd + a 21-year-old with POTE 95 and SPEE 89 is the package a rebuilding club with no identity should accept for a player they may not re-sign. We give from wing surplus (10 wingers on roster) and dump a non-playing asset. Net payroll effect: -$0.30M to us (give $1.10M, get $1.00M). Acceptance uncertain — Savard's 24 points are real production and ATL may want a top prospect instead.

recommendations.current: Zdeno Chara (OTT, D, 27, CHKG 95, TOUG 94, SPEE 91, 31 pts in 22 GP, $1.70M expiring)
recommendations.proposed: TOR 1st round pick + Klesla (TOR, D, 22, POTE 97, SPEE 88, AGIL 87, 13 pts in 25 GP, $0.90M, 2 yrs)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Zdeno Chara from Ottawa for our own 1st rounder and Klesla. He is the only player in the league who simultaneously fixes the checking thinness and the total absence of toughness (our best TOUG is McCabe at 73).
recommendations.rationale: Ottawa is 8-10-2 (22 points) with 24 expiring contracts worth $32.9M, $42.8M payroll, and no competitive direction. They hold all five of their own picks, so they want players, not picks. Klesla at 22 with POTE 97 and 13 points in 25 games is a franchise blueliner for a rebuilding club. Chara at 27 is their best asset but he is expiring — if they cannot re-sign him, a young top-D plus a 1st is the right return. We retain Fischer (24, CHKG 90), Eminger (POTE 99), and Colaiacovo (POTE 99) behind McCabe and Chara. Net payroll effect: +$0.80M (give $0.90M, get $1.70M). Acceptance uncertain — Ottawa may want to keep Chara as their franchise D regardless of the record.

recommendations.current: Sean Avery (LAK, C, 24, FACE 93, CHKG 86, SPEE 88, 3 pts in 24 GP, $400K, 2 yrs)
recommendations.proposed: Tucker (TOR, LW, 29, CHKG 92, PENA 89, TOUG 88, 1 pt in 3 GP, $1.30M, 2 yrs) + Holden (TOR, C, 26, ACCE 84, 0 GP, $1.20M, 1 yr)
recommendations.summary: Acquire Sean Avery from Los Angeles for two undressed surplus players, saving $2.10M in dead payroll while adding a FACE 93 centre on a cheap two-year deal.
recommendations.rationale: Avery's FACE 93, CHKG 86, SPEE 88 at 24 on $400K for two years is the best contract-value player on the board. His production (3 pts in 24 games, 12 MPG) limits him to a bottom-six role, but that is still a massive upgrade over Richards at FACE 70. LA is rebuilding with 13 expiring deals and would value Tucker's CHKG 92 as a veteran presence on a checking line. We give two players who are not dressed (Tucker 3 GP, Holden 0 GP) — pure surplus. Net payroll effect: -$2.10M to us. Acceptance uncertain — LA may see Avery as part of their young core regardless of his production.

recommendations.summary: Koltsov needs to be dressed every night — 12 points in 11 games at 1.09 ppg is too good to sit out.
recommendations.rationale: He has the best points-per-game on the club (1.09) and is playing 9.3 minutes on the fourth line at 23 years old. Alexeev produces at 0.60 ppg and plays every game. Koltsov is outperforming everyone on his line and playing 44% of the schedule. The fourth line getting more ice is the right decision made today, but he also needs to be scratched never.

recommendations.summary: Spacek went from 16 minutes a game to scratched with no injury — understand why and put him back in.
recommendations.rationale: He played 11 games at 16.0 mpg at age 19 with potential 91, then vanished from the lineup with no injury record. That was his band and he was playing well enough to hold it. Whatever the reason, a 19-year-old centre going from a regular to invisible without a medical explanation needs attention.

recommendations.summary: Chistov stays a healthy scratch — 4 points in 14 games has not earned a lineup spot.
recommendations.rationale: His 95 scouting number is an opinion; his production is 0.29 points per game at 9.5 minutes. He is 21 and healthy but has not shown enough to displace Nash (22 pts, 25 games) or Koltsov (12 pts, 11 games at 1.09 ppg). The potential means give him a look later when a roster spot opens, not now.

recommendations.summary: Chlup's role is right for an 18-year-old — 11 minutes on the third line is fair. Watch the morale at 82.
recommendations.rationale: 14 games, 11.1 mpg, 8 points. For a rookie centre at 18, that's a fair introduction. Morale at 82 is the lowest in the under-23 group and worth monitoring — if it drops further, the line assignment may need adjusting to keep him engaged.

recommendations.summary: Safronov has no path through the current defensive depth and that is the honest read.
recommendations.rationale: Zero games, potential 91, but Klesla (25 GP, 14.7 mpg), Eminger (24 GP, 15.0 mpg) and Colaiacovo back on the second pair at 18.7 mpg all block him. He is not being wasted — he is behind three defencemen who are playing better hockey. If one of them goes down, that changes immediately.

recommendations.summary: Leave every line as is for NYI; the room is stable and nothing needs a minutes fix.
recommendations.rationale: Every player's morale is unchanged (`=`) and the roster sits 80-100, so no good player is under his band with a slipping number and no depth man is over his head. The lowest, Aebischer at 80, is our backup goalie at 13 starts behind Belfour (56.0 mpg) — a role/results matter, not something a line change moves.

recommendations.summary: Take Gaborik off the first penalty kill and put Nash on it in his place.
recommendations.rationale: Gaborik is a 92-scoring, 98-speed winger; the first kill needs checking (it sits at a 77 mean and Roberts 86/Fischer already do that). Nash is the checking body on the third line (line checking mean 79) and is already dressed, so this is a special-teams-only swap with no even-strength cost.

recommendations.summary: Leave the first three even-strength lines as they are; they fit their roles.
recommendations.rationale: L1 has a real shutdown D spine (Roberts 86/McCabe 86 checking) around Sundin and Mogilny; L2 is a speed line (Gaborik 98, Afinogenov 96); L3 is the top checking mean at 79. Rebuilding any of them costs chemistry for no role gain.

recommendations.summary: We are thin at centre behind Sundin and can't fix it by moving people around.
recommendations.rationale: Centres are Sundin 90, then Chlup 75 (18), Richards 70, Holden 71 scratched — no true second-line faceoff man. Against a good faceoff club we lose the draws; that is a roster hole for you, not a lineup arrangement.

recommendations.summary: Keep the four lines and both penalty-kill units exactly as they are for Monday at NYI; do not load the checking surplus.
recommendations.rationale: NYI score 2.50 a night and run the league's worst PP at 2-for-57 (3.5%), so there is no offensive threat to match checkers against; the redress plan waits for a hot-scoring club. We're 18-5 on a ten-game run — break nothing.

recommendations.slot: centre, fourth line or extra forward
recommendations.summary: Put Spacek back on the dressing list — a 19-year-old centre with a 91 scouting number who was playing 16 minutes a night should not be sitting healthy.

The shutdown surplus only becomes a line decision when an injury opens a slot.

recommendations.current: Koltsov centre/wing on the fourth line with Spezza and Alexeev
recommendations.proposed: Move Koltsov to the second line at the first opportunity (any forward absence, or a scheduled day off in the lineup order) — 12 points in 11 games is 1.09 a game, the best rate among our regulars.
recommendations.summary: Promote Konstantin Koltsov from the fourth line to the top nine — queued, effective at the first natural opening.
recommendations.rationale: He has earned top-nine minutes by production, but the second line of Richards, Afinogenov and Gaborik is producing and I do not break a working unit on a two-day turnaround before a game we are favoured in. Promotion queued rather than forced.

recommendations.current: Fourth line Spezza/Koltsov/Alexeev carryingChecking assignments it cannot fulfil (60 mean checking, 52 draws)
recommendations.proposed: Use the fourth line as a speed/transition unit — offence-zone looks, short shifts of role clarity — and give the shutdown minutes to the third line (Nash 83, Upshall 87 checking) and the kill units.
recommendations.summary: Stop using the fourth line as a checking unit; it's a speed line and the shutdown work belongs to the third line and the kills.
recommendations.rationale: Composition cannot fix it: no arrangement of this roster puts four checkers on the fourth line without benching production. Usage can: the line's speed (Koltsov 92) is real and the checking is not, so stop asking it for what it doesn't have. Zero chemistry cost — no one moves.

recommendations.current: Centres: Sundin (draws 90), Chlup (75, is 18), Richards (70), Spezza (55), Holden (71, scratched)
recommendations.proposed: Acquire a third/fourth-line centre who wins faceoffs — trade market or waivers. This is the position of need ahead of any forward depth.
recommendations.summary: Roster gap: no true second centre behind Sundin — the draw-winning centre is the position the GM should solve, not the coach.
recommendations.rationale: Behind Sundin's 90 the roster falls off a cliff: 75, 71, 55. Our bottom-two centres will lose the majority of draws against any competent centre and no lineup arrangement fixes that. It is a roster problem, not an arrangement problem — we already carry a surplus of checking, so the ask is specifically a centre who can win a draw, not more grit.

recommendations.summary: No matchup changes for New York — their threats (physical third line, hot stretch) are already covered by the arrangement we dress anyway.
recommendations.rationale: Nothing on their card our current arrangement doesn't already answer: their power play is 2-for-57, their physical third line (Scatchard 89 checking, Simon 95 toughness) is met by our best balanced line (Nash, Upshall, Chlup) already, and their centres outside Bates (94) lose the draw battle to Sundin, Richards and even Chlup on paper. DiPietro (3.57) and Snow (4.00) give nothing that forces a personnel answer. The risk in this game is our own let-down spot, not their roster. Zero chemistry cost.
